label: DAY 8
title: I let 3 bots solve 2,000 mazes. The famous wall trick got stuck 483 times.

scenes.title: Hand on the wall
scenes.caption: right hand on the wall
lines: People say: keep one hand on the wall and you'll escape any maze. I tested it on a thousand mazes. In 483, it walked in circles forever.

scenes.title: The setup
lines: I coded a maze game. Each bot only sees the walls next to it, and the exit is somewhere inside.
Bot one moves at random. Bot two keeps its right hand on the wall. Bot three remembers where it's been, and backs up at dead ends.

scenes.title: No loops
scenes.caption: bot 2, no-loop maze
lines: First, a thousand mazes with no loops.

scenes.title: Escaped: no loops
lines: Random escaped 667 times within my five thousand step limit. The wall trick and the memory bot escaped all thousand.

scenes.sub: 1,000 new mazes, 14 extra walls removed in each
lines: Then, a thousand new mazes with 14 extra walls knocked out of each, so some paths loop.

scenes.title: Escaped: with loops
lines: The wall trick fell to 517. Even the random bot beat it, with 939. Memory still escaped all thousand.

scenes.title: Why it got stuck
lines: In all 483 stuck runs, it never once touched the exit.
Loops can put the exit beside a ring of wall that isn't joined to the outside. The bot circles the outer wall and never reaches it.

scenes.title: Same maze, bot 3
scenes.caption: bot 3: remembers
lines: Same maze where the wall trick got stuck. The memory bot got out in 39 steps.

scenes.text: The trick only works when every wall connects.
scenes.sub: what should these bots try next?
lines: The trick only works when every wall connects to the outside. What should these bots try next? Tell me in the comments.
